tagline: An acoustic platform for observation and organization of living systems: gas vesicles engineered into a programmable interface between ultrasound and biology.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy sees molecular detail but light scattering stops it at tissue depth; X-ray reaches deep but uses ionising radiation; ultrasound penetrates deep without radiation and can even push cells around, but has no molecular specificity. VOYAGE closes that gap with gas vesicles — gas-filled protein nanostructures from aquatic microorganisms, built from GvpA with GvpC reinforcing the outer shell — which scatter ultrasound as genetically encodable contrast agents and buckle at a collapse pressure that can be tuned by engineering GvpC. From that one part the team built four capabilities: GvpC variants with distinct pressure responses as a basis for multiplexed acoustic imaging, a kinase-responsive GvpC that turns phosphorylation into an acoustic signal, latch-based biosensors that report soluble targets, and DARPin- or SpyCatcher-directed vesicles that act as acoustic handles, enriching labelled HEK293T cells roughly tenfold at the side outlet of an acoustophoretic chip and lining them up at pressure antinodes while unlabelled cells sit at the nodes. It won Best Wiki and Best Part Collection because the delivery matched the science: a modular part collection with expression systems for Dolichospermum flos-aquae gas vesicles in mammalian cells and Serratia gas vesicles in E. coli, an accessibility guide for working with gas vesicles on a budget, and ATLAS — a full computational companion spanning all-atom molecular dynamics, three protein design pipelines, a fine-tuned segmentation model and an ultrasound signal model.

dry.frameworks: ATLAS is the most physics-heavy dry lab of the five, in four parts. (1) All-atom molecular dynamics: two neighbouring ribs of 20-25 GvpA from PDB 8GBS in a periodic box, TIP3P water with 150 mM NaCl, CHARMM36 force field, GvpC 33-residue repeats docked on the outer face with full-length termini predicted by AlphaFold2, energy minimisation then restrained equilibration then 6-10 ns production at 310 K in GROMACS 2024, at least three independent runs per variant. Bending stiffness EI is extracted by decomposing each rib's height profile into waves and fitting the equipartition relation where mean squared amplitude falls as the fourth power of wave number, analysed in equal 1.5-2 ns blocks with Welch's t-test across runs, then converted to a critical buckling pressure by classical Timoshenko shell theory at R = 42.5 nm and rib spacing s = 4.9 nm. GvpC binding free energy comes from steered MD (1 nm/ns, force constant 1000 kJ/nm^2) seeding 25 umbrella sampling windows along the centre-of-mass reaction coordinate, recombined by WHAM into a potential of mean force. Wettability was tested by measuring water contact angle on the gas-facing wall face. (2) An in silico evolution pipeline for GvpC: AlphaFold2 predictions of a Serratia GvpA tetramer and a GvpC repeat aligned onto the experimental Dolichospermum GvpA-GvpC complex and repacked, then LigandMPNN redesigning interface residues across four tiers from fully native to all ten positions, with candidates screened by Boltz-2 co-folding, AlphaFold2 in initial-guess mode and PyRosetta relaxation. (3) A de novo binder pipeline: RFdiffusion3 generating backbones against four adjacent GvpA chains, ProteinMPNN designing eight sequences per backbone, AlphaFold2 re-prediction, then filtering on interface PAE, binder pLDDT and RMSD. (4) A biosensor pipeline where RFdiffusion3 designs a blocking latch fused to the binder at freely chosen hotspots, ProteinMPNN redesigns it, and AlphaFold2 scores three states — construct plus GvpA alone (should not bind), construct plus target alone (latch should displace by more than 3.0 A RMSD), and construct plus both (both bound, latch fully dissociated) — with PyRosetta interface delta-G estimates on each bound state.
dry.dataviz: This is the Best Wiki winner and the visualisation is doing real work rather than decoration. Every technical term carries an inline definition on hover (acoustic contrast, acoustic pressure, xAM, acoustophoresis, DARPin, pLDDT, i_pAE), and every computational tool gets an 'Explore this software' panel explaining what it is, how it works and what its published benchmarks are — so a reader can follow the pipeline without already knowing LigandMPNN or CellSAM. Structures are interactive: a 'View in 3D' control turns the progression from one GvpA, to a rib inside its cryo-EM density (EMD-14238), to the 13,450-copy vesicle, to the GvpC cage; MD trajectories play as interactive animations of the wall rippling; and biosensor constructs can be rotated with and without bound GFP. The GVSAM results are presented as a ten-image gallery where the reader switches each test image between raw, ground truth, GVSAM prediction with true positives, false positives and false negatives marked, and the base CellSAM prediction — which lets a sceptic check the model rather than take the F1 score on trust. Design pipelines appear as schematic flow diagrams, and the binder filtering is shown as KDE plots overlaying all 1,429 designs against the 13 accepted ones on each metric, making visible that many designs pass individual gates while almost none pass all three.
dry.datascience: The honesty is the distinguishing feature. The MD model predicts a 1.63-fold stiffness increase from truncated GvpC against 1.48-fold measured experimentally — close — but its absolute collapse pressure estimate of 124-137 kPa without GvpC sits well below the experimental 195 kPa, and the team states plainly that ATLAS is therefore suited to ranking variants rather than predicting absolute pressures, because a whole vesicle is not an idealised wall patch. The umbrella sampling gives 43.5 kJ/mol to remove one GvpC repeat (about 17 k_B T at 310 K) and notes that the free energy plateaus once the repeat has moved 0.55 nm, when only 24% of original atom contacts remain, so most of the cost is paid before the last contacts break. The wetting hypothesis was tested and rejected on its merits: 122.8 degrees without GvpC against 122.2 with, a 0.6-degree difference against the roughly 6 degrees a condensation mechanism would require. Screening thresholds were calibrated against controls rather than chosen by feel — the redesigned sequences were run alongside native Serratia GvpC repeat 3 and nine negative controls, and of all metrics tested only AlphaFold2 interface PAE separated them cleanly (135 of 200 designs passed the 12.0 gate, all nine negative controls failed, the native repeat passed at 11.42), with the team stating explicitly that only that one threshold is calibrated and the other three are a priori safeguards whose predictive value is unproven. PyRosetta interface energies are reported but excluded from selection because they did not discriminate the controls. GVSAM's evaluation was adapted to the problem: intersection over union is unsuitable for objects this small because a one-pixel shift wrecks it, so a hit requires the annotated box centre to lie inside the prediction within 2 px and the areas to differ by at most fourfold, each annotation matchable once, highest-scoring first — with recall, precision and F1 pooled across images and 95% confidence intervals bootstrapped over images. They report F1 rising from 0.2% (base CellSAM) to 42% (GVSAM) with false positives down 97%, and openly diagnose overfitting: validation loss bottomed at epoch 6 while training loss kept falling, so that checkpoint was taken. Two team members annotated independently to reduce single-annotator bias, images of deliberately varying quality and images with no vesicles at all were kept for robustness, and the 108 annotated images were split 70/20/10 at image level with vesicle and non-vesicle images split separately. Ultrasound analysis in GAS uses median intensity and median absolute deviation rather than mean and standard deviation because ultrasound speckle makes single-pixel brightness fluctuate with intensity, with background subtracted as the median recorded after all vesicles were destroyed, and collapse pressure taken as P50 from a four-parameter regression fit (R-squared above 0.99 on all curves).
dry.software: ATLAS ships as a documented end-to-end pipeline with its own comprehensive user guide, covering the MD characterisation route, the GvpC in silico evolution pipeline and the de novo binder and biosensor design pipelines. GVSAM is a fine-tuned derivative of CellSAM (itself built on Meta's Segment Anything Model with an Anchor DETR based CellFinder detector and a ViT-B encoder) retrained to detect gas vesicle clusters rather than whole cells, trained with Dice plus binary cross-entropy with logits, batch size 3, learning rate 1e-4 (backbone 1e-5), weight decay 1e-4, annotated in napari and converted to bounding boxes by a Python script, with 90 and 270 degree rotation augmentation to cope with only 108 images. GAS is the physics-informed fitting model that converts raw cross-amplitude-modulation ultrasound data into pressure-dependent signal curves. On the wet side the team released the VOYAGE part collection (expression systems for D. flos-aquae gas vesicles in mammalian cells and Serratia gas vesicles in E. coli, plus characterisation and purification parts), an extensive collection of optimised gas vesicle protocols including AFM and darkfield imaging, and an accessibility guide for working with gas vesicles on a budget — which includes using the open-source 3D-printed OpenFlexure microscope for darkfield imaging of purified vesicles and live-cell imaging of producers, explicitly so that teams with limited resources can replicate the work. The Fail Forward Guide is the fourth released artefact.
stack: CellSAM / Segment Anything Model (fine-tuned as GVSAM)
Verasonics Vantage NXT (v2.3.3), 5.2 MHz linear probe, xAM sequence
techniques: Thermal-fluctuation spectrum analysis to extract bending stiffness
Timoshenko shell theory conversion of stiffness to buckling pressure
Potential of mean force / binding free energy calculation
Contact-angle measurement to test a wetting collapse mechanism
Cross-species structural templating justified by sequence identity and repeat periodicity
Tiered interface redesign (native through full redesign)
Multi-state conditional scoring of a conformational switch
Transfer learning / fine-tuning a segmentation foundation model on 108 images
Position-and-size matching criterion in place of IoU for small objects
Robust statistics (median, MAD) against ultrasound speckle
Cross-amplitude modulation nonlinear ultrasound imaging with hydrophone calibration
Four-parameter regression for P50 collapse pressure
Acoustophoretic cell sorting and standing-wave spatial patterning

good.publicEngagement: Heidelberg's education programme, Fail Forward, takes error culture in science as its subject rather than synthetic biology content, which makes it unusually distinctive. The centrepiece is the Error Bar, billed as 'a night of scientific f*ck ups': around 80 students and researchers in the university's student bar in July, with successful professionals telling their own stories of things going wrong and what they learned. It was deliberately not a lecture — a short presentation introduced structural problems including publication bias against negative results and mental health stressors in academia, then interactive activities invited participants to share their own experiences, and recreation therapist Brady Hughes ran a workshop on distinguishing a fiasco from a crisis, reappraising situations and using grounding exercises, ending with the group shredding their recent failures together. A panel discussion with around 120 participants extended the theme from personal to institutional failure in the healthcare system, bringing researchers, healthcare professionals, patient advocates and the public into one room, with one panellist making the publication-bias argument in concrete terms: unpublished negative studies mean the same approach gets tried repeatedly, wasting resources and re-exposing participants to risk. All of it was distilled into the Fail Forward Guide, which includes background on failure in academia, expert interviews, and a tutorial for hosting your own Error Bar anywhere in the world — and the team has already committed to making the Error Bar recurring, with an open-mic session planned and PIs who missed it asking to join the next one. Alongside this they ran a Science Cinema with the local student cinema Unikino Heidelberg (over 70 participants for GATTACA, followed by a presentation and open discussion on how realistic the scenario is and which elements of that society we can already find in our own), a documentary screening with gynaecologist Dr Kathrin Haßdenteufel providing medical context and a Q&A (40 participants, every seat taken), a Science Pub Quiz, a Science Slam, school workshops, a laboratory summer school, a lecture series, and a full-day alumni event at the Marsilius-Kolleg bringing around 45 current and former iGEM Heidelberg members from every year the university has competed.
good.ihp: The clearest example of stakeholder input changing method rather than framing came from Prof Dr Frauke Gräter, interviewed on modelling strategy. The team first built exactly what she proposed — two Martini coarse-grained sheets with gas between them, tested at different pressures — and it taught them something by failing: the flat patch collapsed even without any applied pressure, because it lacks the closed curved geometry that holds a real vesicle open. That killed the approach and, building on her point that relative differences are what matter for ranking and that a small wall section is representative, they switched to measuring bending stiffness on an all-atom repeating patch and converting it through shell theory. Her warning about sampling is why they chose bending rather than stretching as the primary measurement, ran every simulation at least three times and compared several GvpC variants rather than only wild type; her advice on pulling speed went into the steered MD, where they pulled at several speeds and used only runs in which GvpC genuinely came off. They also tried her suggested coarse-grained model as a fast pre-screen, found it could not distinguish the variants, and state that every reported result therefore comes from all-atom simulation. Elsewhere: Prof Pfeifer warned that GvpA is highly conserved and vulnerable to mutation, redirecting the whole engineering effort onto GvpC as the modular target, and explained which accessory genes the expression constructs needed. Dr Huber's feedback on how long even one sub-idea takes changed how many aspects they attempted and forced explicit prioritisation. A stakeholder conversation led them to replace the D. flos-aquae / P. megaterium expression mix with a Serratia-based cassette in E. coli, which is what finally gave them expression and purification and set the host for everything downstream. Protein design expert Paul Kittner diagnosed a real failure mode: hallucination tools like BindCraft are biased toward hydrophobic interfaces because their structure predictors are trained on natural ones, and GvpA's outward-facing surface is hydrophilic — he advised adding a custom penalty term to the generation loss, which worked and let them target the hydrophilic face, and also pointed them to diffusion models as less biased, which is why RFdiffusion3 became the backbone generator. Dr Michael Jendrusch told them bluntly that no existing pipeline suited their biosensing goal and sketched the binder-plus-latch architecture they built, including the multi-state scoring step and the advice to screen with pooled assays and Twist Oligo Pools rather than testing candidates individually. Prof Dr Karl Rohr's advice is why GVSAM fine-tunes CellSAM rather than training from scratch. Mentor Molina Ramirez moved from interview subject to collaborator, supervising imaging, adapting the xAM script to their specific transducer, and advising them to use beamformed rather than pixel data and median rather than mean normalisation to suppress outliers. Prof Dr Georg Schmitz gave them a falsifiable clinical test — look first with the transducer you already have at frequencies close to clinical scanners, and only go higher if nothing appears — which they followed and passed at 5-7 MHz. Dr Lakshmanan's practical warnings (closing a low-quality tube cap can generate enough pressure to collapse vesicles) shaped handling, and her advice to modify GvpC termini shaped the latch design.
good.realWorld: The target application is monitoring engineered cell therapies, chosen because the alternatives are genuinely inadequate: PET tracking needs suitable radioactive tracers and costly specialised equipment, with each scan requiring tracer administration so measurements are days apart rather than continuous; bioluminescence imaging needs no such infrastructure but cannot penetrate patient tissue; and biopsy is invasive, reports only the sampled site, and cannot show how therapeutic cells redistribute. Ultrasound is comparatively inexpensive, widely available and needs no ionising radiation or tracer, which is the whole argument for a genetically encoded acoustic reporter. Crucially they tested the frequency question rather than assuming it: all measurements were made at 5-7 MHz, a range clinical scanners use, so purified vesicles, GV-expressing bacteria and mammalian cells were all detected as clear scattering signals against a degassed negative control without resorting to high frequencies that would limit penetration depth — while stating openly that whether a therapeutic cell can accumulate enough vesicles for a detectable in vivo signal remains to be established. The team has patent work on a modular, reversible acoustic label: because interchangeable binding proteins attach vesicles to a chosen target, the target's acoustic properties change without genetically modifying it, which matters for cell-therapy manufacturing where the product must not be altered. Named next steps are specific — test one ATLAS binder against a marker with existing clinical use such as HER2 or PD-L1, and test two gas vesicle variants with distinct collapse pressures in a tissue-mimicking phantom to establish whether both signals can be read in one measurement, with a published liver phantom protocol cited as a starting point — plus quantifying sorting efficiency and validating cell viability after label removal. A collaboration with PHOENICS is sketched on shared mechanism: the PHOENICS cell computes through phosphorylation and the GvpC sensor turns phosphorylation into ultrasound, so together they would make an engineered cell's internal decision readable from outside the body.

images.caption: The complete in silico GvpC redesign pipeline: the template is split into interface and structural residues, interface redesign is deep-learning-guided with LigandMPNN while structural residues are chosen rationally, candidates are predicted and filtered by structure predictors and physical constraints, and validated variants feed back to retune the gating strategy.

Interface PAE distribution across all 1,429 de novo GvpA binder designs (orange) against the 13 accepted ones (blue). Nearly half of all designs failed on this metric alone, which is why the pipeline reports each gate separately rather than a single composite score.

Recall, precision and F1 with bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals for GVSAM against the base CellSAM model on 10 held-out microscopy images containing 114 annotated gas vesicle clusters — F1 rose from 0.2% to 42% after fine-tuning on just 108 annotated images, with false positives down 97%.

The Error Bar, 'a night of scientific f*ck ups': around 80 students and researchers in the university student bar hearing established scientists talk about their own failures, with interactive activities and a workshop on distinguishing a fiasco from a crisis.

gemsTakeaway: The transferable dry-lab habit is calibrating your filters against negative controls before you trust them: Heidelberg ran nine deliberately bad sequences plus the real binder through the identical pipeline, found that only AlphaFold2 interface PAE separated them, said so, and refused to select on the metrics that failed the test — a discipline that costs nothing but compute and turns a pile of prediction scores into an actual decision rule. On the human side, copy Fail Forward: an evening where senior scientists tell students about their own failures, plus a written guide that includes instructions for running the event yourself. For a high-school-plus research centre whose students will mostly meet failure before success, an institutional format that makes failure discussable is worth more than another outreach workshop — and the guide means you can run it next term without inventing it.
